list.title: Lateral Flow Tests (Antigen Tests):
list.snippet: These tests are less sensitive and are more likely to turn negative sooner than PCR tests after the initial infection. However, a single negative antigen test may not be enough to rule out infection, particularly if symptoms are present. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (.gov) and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention | CDC recommend multiple negative antigen tests (e.g., two negative tests for symptomatic individuals or three negative tests) to be more confident in the results, says the CDC.
